player_action: I swing from the chandelier and kick the bandit into the fireplace. What's the roll?
game_state: Tavern brawl; a chandelier hangs 10 ft up, fireplace behind the bandit.
correct_ruling: The SRD has no specific chandelier-swing rule. The DM decides how to resolve it, e.g. a Jump or Climb check to grab and swing, then a bull rush or similar opposed check to push the bandit, with any fire damage set by the DM.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SkillsI/II (Jump, Climb); CombatII.rtf > Bull Rush; no specific rule for the stunt
common_wrong_rulings: Inventing a precise 'swing' rule and presenting it as RAW

player_action: My last DM always gave me advantage when I attacked from higher ground, so roll twice and take the higher.
game_state: PC standing on a table, attacking an orc on the floor.
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no advantage mechanic. Attacking from higher ground grants a +1 bonus on melee attack rolls. Prior DM house rules don't bind this table.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 CombatII.rtf > Combat Modifiers table (higher ground +1 melee)

player_action: I take the Dodge action and everyone has disadvantage against me.
game_state: Fighter in melee.
correct_ruling: That's 5th edition. 3.5 has no Dodge action or disadvantage. The closest options are fighting defensively (-4 attack, +2 dodge AC) or the total defense standard action (+4 dodge AC, no attacks).
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 CombatII.rtf > Fighting Defensively; Total Defense
common_wrong_rulings: Allowing the 5e Dodge action as written

player_action: It's only realistic that a crossbow bolt to the neck kills him outright. I crit, so he's dead.
game_state: PC crits a 40 hp ogre with a light crossbow for 14 damage.
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no called shots or instant-kill crits (aside from specific effects like vorpal or death attacks). A critical hit multiplies damage; the ogre takes 14 and is still up.
common_wrong_rulings: Allowing a called-shot penalty system as RAW

player_action: The rules say a natural 20 on a save always succeeds, so a natural 20 on my Diplomacy check makes the king agree.
game_state: Diplomacy check to change a hostile king's attitude.
correct_ruling: Natural 20 auto-success applies to attack rolls and saving throws, not skill checks. Diplomacy changes an NPC's attitude per the attitude table; it doesn't mind-control.
common_wrong_rulings: Treating nat 20 as automatic success on any d20 roll

player_action: I want to cut the rope bridge while the hobgoblins are crossing. How many hits?
game_state: Rope bridge, ropes are the anchor points.
correct_ruling: The SRD gives hardness and hit points for rope (0 hardness, 2 hp) and rules for sundering/breaking objects, but how many ropes must be cut and what happens to the bridge are the DM's call.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 CombatII.rtf > Attack an Object; Exploration > Breaking and Entering (substance hardness/hp)
common_wrong_rulings: Declaring a fixed number of hits as RAW
confidence_note: Rope 0 hardness / 2 hp recalled from the object hardness table; the scored point is only that bridge collapse is DM adjudication.

player_action: Inspiration! I did a cool thing, so I get to reroll.
game_state: Bard just failed a save.
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no inspiration/reroll mechanic (the bard's inspire courage is a different ability). The failed save stands unless a specific feat, item, or class feature allows a reroll.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 (no such mechanic); ClassesI.rtf > Bard > Bardic Music

player_action: Can I use prestidigitation to make the duke's soup taste like rotten fish, and does he notice it's magic?
game_state: Formal dinner; PC wizard knows prestidigitation.
correct_ruling: Prestidigitation can flavor nonliving material, so the soup can taste bad. Whether the duke notices the casting depends on Spellcraft/Spot and the DM's judgment of the scene; the rules don't automatically reveal it.
common_wrong_rulings: Spellcasting is automatically noticed by everyone
confidence_note: 3.5 has no explicit rule that casting is noticed; noticing via Spot/Spellcraft is standard adjudication but not codified.

player_action: Short rest! We take an hour and I spend Hit Dice to heal.
game_state: Party after a fight, mid-dungeon.
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no short rests or Hit Dice spending. Natural healing is 1 hp per character level per full night's rest (8 hours); 2 per level for a full day of complete bed rest.

player_action: In Pathfinder combat maneuvers use CMB vs CMD, so I trip using my CMB against his CMD of 15.
game_state: 3.5 game; fighter trying to trip an orc.
correct_ruling: 3.5 doesn't use CMB/CMD. A trip is a melee touch attack, then an opposed Strength check (defender may use Dex if higher), with size modifiers; failure lets the defender try to trip you back.
common_wrong_rulings: Trip as Athletics vs Acrobatics (5e shove)

player_action: I try to convince the gate guard that we're merchants. What's the DC?
game_state: Guard is indifferent, has a Sense Motive modifier of +2.
correct_ruling: Bluff is opposed by the guard's Sense Motive, not a fixed DC. The DM sets circumstance modifiers based on how believable the lie is and how much the guard wants to believe it.

player_action: We find a secret door. Can I tell what's behind it by putting my ear to it — what's the Listen DC through stone?
game_state: 1-foot-thick stone door; orcs talking quietly beyond.
correct_ruling: Listen has modifiers for listening through a door (+5 DC) and through a stone wall (+15 per foot). The DM decides whether this door counts as a door or as stone wall, and sets the base DC for the conversation (people talking is about DC 0).
confidence_note: Listen modifiers (+5 through door, +15 per foot of stone, DC 0 talking) are from memory of the Listen table; scoring only checks for Listen and DM judgment.

player_action: I'm the player, I know the rule: a 5-foot step never provokes, so I'll 5-foot step and then move my full 30.
game_state: Fighter in melee with a goblin, wants to step away then move.
correct_ruling: A 5-foot step is only allowed in a round in which you don't otherwise move. You can't take a 5-foot step and also take a move action to move.

player_action: I want to craft a fake royal seal so we can forge orders. What's my check?
game_state: Rogue with Forgery and Craft skills.
correct_ruling: Forgery covers forging documents and is opposed by Forgery checks of readers; it requires a sample of the handwriting/seal for best results. How the physical seal is made (e.g., Craft) and its DC are for the DM to set.
confidence_note: Forgery is opposed by the reader's Forgery check per SRD; the seal-crafting part is unspecified.

player_action: The PHB says sneak attack works on anything with a body, so I sneak attack the zombie.
game_state: Rogue flanking a human zombie (undead).
correct_ruling: Undead are immune to sneak attack (immune to critical hits/precision damage) in 3.5. The rogue deals normal weapon damage only.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 ClassesI.rtf > Rogue > Sneak Attack; TypesSubtypes.rtf > Undead traits
common_wrong_rulings: Allowing sneak attack on undead (Pathfinder/5e behavior)

player_action: How long does it take to dig a pit trap in this dirt floor?
game_state: Party has shovels, wants a 10-ft-deep pit.
correct_ruling: The core SRD has no general digging-rate rule. The DM decides the time (possibly using Strength or Craft checks).
common_wrong_rulings: Quoting an invented RAW digging rate as authoritative
confidence_note: I believe the core SRD has no digging rate (there are rules in other books); flag in case an SRD section covers it.

player_action: I'm a wizard so I can cast in full plate — the armor is just for show, there's no real penalty.
game_state: Wizard in full plate casting magic missile (somatic component).
correct_ruling: Full plate carries a 35% arcane spell failure chance for spells with somatic components. Roll d%; on 35 or less the spell fails and is lost.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 Equipment.rtf > Armor table; Arcane Spell Failure
common_wrong_rulings: Wizards can't cast at all in armor

player_action: I disguise myself as the city's bishop. The guards know him personally — what's the modifier?
game_state: PC with Disguise; guards familiar with the bishop.
correct_ruling: Disguise gives viewers who know the person a bonus on their Spot check (recognition vs friends/associates per the familiarity table). The exact circumstances (lighting, distance, behavior) are DM judgment.
common_wrong_rulings: Disguise is an automatic success vs strangers and friends alike
confidence_note: Familiarity bonuses (+4 recognizes, +6 friends, +8 close friends, +10 intimate) recalled from memory; not scored.

player_action: Everyone gets a free 'bonus action' in this edition, so I drink a potion as a bonus action and still attack twice.
game_state: Fighter with BAB +6 wants a full attack and a potion in the same round.
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no bonus action. Drinking a potion is a standard action that provokes attacks of opportunity; a full attack is a full-round action. You can't do both in one round.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 CombatII.rtf > Actions in Combat table; MagicItems > Potions

player_action: The ceiling has a hole; can I use fly's flight to carry the unconscious paladin up through it? He's in full plate.
game_state: Wizard under fly; paladin weighs ~250 lb with gear; wizard Str 10.
correct_ruling: Fly lets a subject fly at its speed, with speed reduced under a medium or heavy load. Carrying limits still apply: 250 lb exceeds a Str 10 maximum heavy load (100 lb), so he can't carry it in flight; at most he could lift 200 lb off the ground and stagger. Any creative workaround is DM adjudication.
confidence_note: Recalled: 3.5 fly gives 60 ft speed (40 ft in medium/heavy armor or with a medium/heavy load); not re-checked against SRD text. The weight-cap conclusion (can't exceed max heavy load) is solid.
